rows.rule: The PAYE Regulations define emoluments to include office/employment income, pensions, cash gratuities and benefits in kind. Payment includes credit to an account on which the employee can draw. Regulation 3 requires withholding even without an assessment and even where the payment relates to another assessment year. Do not postpone withholding solely because a bonus relates to earlier service. [Regulations 2–3](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/1989s114/1989s114(01-07-23).pdf).

rows.rule: Regulation 8(1) uses gross emoluments, the employee's code and the official table on each payday. **If neither the required allowances certificate nor the applicable leaver certificate has been lodged, regulation 8(2) requires code X.** Do not substitute a guessed personal allowance or zero withholding while awaiting a code. Regulation 8(3) adds the proportionate money value of benefits to gross emoluments; valuation and exemptions require separate evidence. A Commissioner direction under 8(4) can specify a different deduction. An agreement not to deduct cannot override the duty. rows.rule: For partial weekly/monthly service, the notes divide pay by days worked, look up the daily amount and multiply that daily tax by the days worked. They use weekly tables for fortnightly/four-weekly pay (divide and multiply by two/four), monthly tables for quarterly/half-yearly pay (three/six), and annual tables for annual pay. rows.rule: Regulation 11(3) permits the Commissioner, at discretion, to increase late-paid PAYE by **2% for each month of delay, compounded**. This is not an automatic flat 2% penalty, and these PAYE regulations do not establish the SI penalty. rows.rule: Section 7(1) places initial payment responsibility for both the employer's and the insured employee's contribution on the employer, unless regulations prescribe otherwise. **The employer's share cannot be deducted from wages or otherwise recovered from the employee, even by agreement.** Recovery of the employee's share is subject to the regulations and section 7(3): where there is no wage or other monetary remuneration from any person in respect of the employment, recovery is prohibited; where the employer pays wages, recovery must be by deduction from them. Do not assume unpaid deductions can be collected in any later payroll without checking the recovery rules. [Social Security (Insurance) Act, section 7(1)–(3)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/social-security/1955-14/1955-14(01-07-25).pdf).

rows.rule: The claim requires all SI and PAYE amounts to have been paid on the due date under 17A(2); 17A(6) identifies the due date as on or before the 15th of the following month. Do not treat arrears cleared at year-end as automatically satisfying timely payment. If employer contributions for an employee total less than £100, that employee's credit is restricted to the actual total. Once granted, the credit offsets employer contribution liabilities in the following year. It is not a current employee deduction or an automatic income-tax refund. [Regulation 17A(2)–(6)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/social-security/1955.08.04-5/1955.08.04-5(01-07-15).pdf).

rows.rule: **Example:** an eligible employer never exceeds eight employees. Seven employees each generated at least £100 of employer contributions; the eighth generated £60. Subject to timely-payment and claim conditions, the credit is **7 × £100 + £60 = £760**, below the £1,000 cap, for offset in the following year once granted. A continuing business that reached eleven employees fails the stated headcount condition even if it ended the year with eight. A first-year business with fifteen qualifying employees, each with at least £100 employer contributions, has a provisional **£1,500** credit under the enlarged limit. These examples assume confirmed employee counts; staff turnover/counting details and the current claim form/channel remain unverified.

rows.rule:
1. Confirm class, pay frequency, full/partial period, and earnings base before selecting a schedule.
2. For a confirmed full-month ordinary class with an established contribution liability, compute employee `min(176.76, max(62.11, earnings × 10%))` and employer `min(243.65, max(138.55, earnings × 18%))`.
3. Use the employee's tax code and correct-year official tax tables for PAYE. Contribution rates are not income-tax rates.
4. Reconcile gross wages, PAYE, employee contributions, other deductions, net wages and employer cost separately.
5. Reconcile payroll totals to remittances and the annual return. Never multiply a rounded monthly cap to substitute for an official annual table.

rows.rule: Choose special benefit Chapter first, money/moneysworth, employment/family link, exclusions and distinct SI/wage base
rows.assertion: Schedule 7 paragraph 1 includes salary/wages/fees, money or money's-worth employment profits and other emoluments. Choose the applicable Chapter before valuing a benefit; paragraph 38 excludes from the residual Chapter benefits covered by another Chapter or its stated exception. Keep the provider, recipient/family connection, reason for provision, dates, costs, market/rental evidence and amounts made good. The tax value is not automatically cash wages, a social-insurance earnings base or permission to deduct the employer's cost from wages. [Income Tax Act, Schedule 7 paragraphs 1, 37–38 and 40–46](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2010-21/2010-21(23-03-26).pdf).

rows.rule: Expenses exceed qualifying paid-away amount; cash/noncash vouchers/cards, exclusions/timing/value and no double counting
rows.assertion: **Expenses, vouchers and cards:** paragraph 6 charges the employment-expense payment to the extent it exceeds expenses paid away wholly, exclusively and necessarily in the course of the employment. Under paragraph 7 a qualifying cash voucher is valued at the money for which it can be exchanged. Paragraph 8 values a qualifying non-cash voucher at provision cost less employee reimbursement; paragraphs 9–10 give the separate credit-token cost rule. Retain the employment/family, receipt/appropriation, public-terms exclusions and statutory timing conditions, including the later-cost/receipt rule and cheque-voucher use/posting rule. Paragraph 11 prevents double counting the resulting money/goods/services, with its employment-expense qualification. Do not value every voucher at face value or tax both voucher and redeemed goods. [Schedule 7 paragraphs 6–11](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2010-21/2010-21(23-03-26).pdf).

rows.rule: Accommodation rental/actual-higher rent/employee payment/nil, shared allocation, specific skills four-year exception and declaration
rows.assertion: **Living accommodation:** where Chapter 4 applies, paragraphs 14–17 use the rental value for the taxable period, substituting the provider's higher actual rent where required, less the employee's properly attributable payment; the result is nil if that payment meets/exceeds rental value. Annual value is the specified reasonable year-to-year rent with tenant charges and landlord repairs/insurance assumptions. Shared accommodation uses a just-and-reasonable split of one total cash equivalent, not the full value charged to every occupant. Paragraph 18 sends annual-value disputes to the Tribunal. The paragraph 13 specific-employee exception needs the relocation, former-home distance, Commissioner-determined skills and employer-application conditions, change notification and annual benefit declaration. It lasts four years from Gibraltar employment commencement and once per employee; relocation alone is not an exemption. [Schedule 7 paragraphs 12–19](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2010-21/2010-21(23-03-26).pdf).

rows.rule: Car/van definitions,3500kg, private use,25% first4years/0%, provision-market comparator, all pool conditions and shared-use rule; paragraph28 fuel90%/madegood, covered provision routes and printed paragraph23 reference
rows.assertion: **Cars and vans:** first establish employment-related availability without a property transfer and private use under paragraphs 20–23, including the vehicle definitions (a van's design weight is at most 3,500 kilograms). Private use is presumed unless prohibited by the terms and not actually made. Paragraph 26 uses 25% per annum of employer cost for each of the first four years of availability, then 0%; for a vehicle the provider does not purchase, use the higher provision cost/market value, less amounts made good. A cash alternative alone does not trigger earnings under paragraph 24. The pool exception requires all paragraph 27 conditions, including actual multiple use, no ordinarily exclusive user, merely incidental private use and the overnight-location restriction. Paragraph 39 requires a separate calculation then just-and-reasonable reduction for qualifying shared private-use cars. For employment-provided car fuel within paragraph 28’s chargeability condition, value is 90% of employer fuel cost less amounts made good. Provision includes discharged fuel liabilities, voucher/card fuel or money spent on fuel, and fuel-expense payments; retain the paragraph’s printed paragraph-23 reference rather than silently substituting another. No unsupported partial-year convention or fuel/private-use exemption is assumed here. [Schedule 7 paragraphs 20–28 and 39](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2010-21/2010-21(23-03-26).pdf).

rows.rule: Loan scope/comparable unconnected interest less paid, relief exception,£1000 expense-advance/sixmonth/records, allocation/writeoff/death
rows.assertion: **Employment-related loans:** paragraphs 29–31 include credit and arranging/guaranteeing/facilitating a loan, the defined employer/connected-provider and recipient categories, and the actual outstanding/employment period. The taxable cheap-loan value is comparable interest from an unconnected bank/building society on similar non-interest terms minus interest actually paid. No UK official interest rate or universal loan-size exemption is imported. Paragraph 32 excludes the loan to the extent hypothetical interest qualifies for the specified tax relief/trading deduction. Paragraph 33's necessary/overnight-expense advance exception needs the £1,000 outstanding limit throughout the year, spending within six months and regular accounting, with its expense definitions. Paragraph 34 apportions joint-loan value justly/reasonably. Write-off under paragraph 35 is earnings on release/write-off, subject to paragraph 36's death rules; it is not merely another year's interest benefit. [Schedule 7 paragraphs 29–36](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2010-21/2010-21(23-03-26).pdf).

rows.rule: Residual provision cost, madegood,20% nonland asset comparator, actual hire/additional expense and market transfer; no car double-rule
rows.assertion: **Residual benefits and assets:** paragraphs 40–41 use provision expense, including a proper proportion of shared costs, less the employee's reimbursement. Paragraph 42 separately values an asset made available without transfer at the higher annual-use value or rent/hire, plus additional expenses; annual-use value is rental value for land or 20% of the relevant initial market value for other assets. Paragraph 43 uses market value at transfer for a used/depreciated asset; paragraph 45 defines open-market value. Do not substitute book value or employer cost for that transfer rule, or use the residual asset percentage for a car covered by Chapter 5. A private health-policy benefit and any personal health-insurance deduction need separate charging and deduction analyses. [Schedule 7 paragraphs 37–46](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2010-21/2010-21(23-03-26).pdf); [Allowances Rules 20A–20B](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/1992s016/1992s016(23-03-26).pdf).

rows.rule: Nonapproved pension charge, no double charge and broken rule3(17) definition distinguished from administrative FAQ
rows.assertion: **Pension caution:** paragraph 48 charges employer contributions to its non-approved personal-pension arrangements, without double charging the same income. Its definition points to Allowances rule 3(17), whose current printed text instead concerns approved-fund investment income. The employee FAQ states its administrative distinction between approved occupational/personal schemes and retirement annuity contracts; that statement does not repair the statutory cross-reference or establish every actual scheme's treatment. Keep approval and scheme documents and the exact unresolved reference; do not claim a blanket employee exemption from the employer's deduction or a scheme's label. rows.rule: Separate explicit synthetic valuations500/500/8000, fuel1500, loan1500,18000/2700; no combined tax or SI result
rows.assertion: **Independent valuation illustrations:** assume every stated charging, timing and non-exemption condition is established. An expense payment of £2,000 against £1,500 paid away on the qualifying employment expenses leaves £500. A non-cash voucher with £600 provision cost and £100 made good gives £500. A full first-year employer-owned qualifying car costing £40,000 with £2,000 made good gives £8,000. For a separate established paragraph-28 fuel case, £2,000 employer fuel cost and £300 made good give £1,500. A distinct £50,000 full-year loan with independently evidenced 5% comparable interest and £1,000 paid gives £1,500; 5% is an assumed comparable rate, not a statutory rate. With established full-year rental value £18,000, provider rent £24,000 and employee payment £6,000, the accommodation value is £18,000. A separate residual non-car asset with relevant market value £10,000, hire £2,500, additional expense £300 and employee reimbursement £100 gives £2,700. These are separate benefit-base examples before any aggregate threshold, applicable deduction or PAYE calculation.

rows.assertion: Paragraph 73 states that no return/tax is required for total employee benefits **less than/below £250** in an assessment year, subject to any replacement sum specified by legal notice. The current employee FAQ instead says the “first £250” is exempt. Those are different formulations: this Guide does not automatically subtract £250 from every larger benefit package or decide the exact-£250 boundary from the FAQ. Keep the annual aggregate, specific exceptions and the operative primary wording; a case affected by that difference needs the applicable determination. rows.rule: Employer election20%/29% on relevant established whole benefit value and no extra employee tax on employer-paid tax; separate1000/20000 examples200/5800
rows.assertion: Under paragraph 74 the employer can elect to pay the employee's benefit tax, with no additional employee tax on the employer-paid tax itself. The printed rates apply to the otherwise taxable benefit value: 20% where the value is between £250 and £15,000, and 29% where it is above £15,000. The latter is not described as a marginal rate on only the excess. With independently established otherwise taxable values of £1,000 and, in a separate case, £20,000, tax is £200 and £5,800. These assumptions do not resolve paragraph 73's aggregate/boundary issue or permit deducting the employer's tax from wages. The current employer page lists P10/P10A for benefits and employer-paid benefit tax and a 31 July annual reporting date; retain the actual form year, election, return and payment evidence. [Schedule 7 paragraph 74](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2010-21/2010-21(23-03-26).pdf); [employer reporting FAQ](https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/income-tax-office/employers-and-trusts/employers).

rows.rule: Dispensation statement/notice/scope, expense restriction, revocation and30day affected-return duty; no self approval
rows.assertion: For a dispensation, paragraphs 70–72 require a statement of the relevant payments/benefits/arrangements and the Commissioner's notice agreeing no additional tax is payable; it is not self-approved. Paragraph 75 limits the relief/reporting effect to covered facts, prevents the specified further employment-expense allowance and keeps the dispensation in force until written revocation. Paragraphs 76–78 permit revocation from its original or a later date, restoring the relevant liabilities and requiring the affected returns within 30 days of the notice unless a longer period is allowed in writing. Keep the statement, notice, covered scope, changes and revocation record. A published FAQ or a requested dispensation is not that notice. rows.rule: Court-recovery employer sums satisfy contributions and cannot be recovered from insured person; ordinary missed-wage question distinct
rows.assertion: Social Insurance regulation 7 concerns the court-recovery circumstances and related sums payable to the Fund. Paragraph (6) expressly says an employer's payment under those provisions satisfies unpaid contributions and **no part is recoverable from the insured person**. That is a positive restriction for those sums, not a general answer authorising collection of an ordinary missed employee deduction from later wages. The Act's section 7 restrictions and the unresolved ordinary recovery mechanism remain as stated above. Keep the order, contribution period, employer payment and employee deductions distinct. [SI regulation 7(1)–(8), especially 7(6)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/social-security/1955.08.04-5/1955.08.04-5(01-07-15).pdf).

Examples of this include, Health Insurance, Food Vouchers, Clothing Allowances or even a Vehicle Purchased by the Employer for an Employee’s private use. This value will be included as part of your taxable income at assessment time, and could increase your tax liability. However the
